Washing hands

Fill a washing-up bowl with water and soap and share it for the whole time. Soap and water works better than hand sanitiser. Anyone with diarrhoea uses their own bowl. Don't use water for showers or baths.
If the bottled water runs out

Only if nothing safe is left: collect rainwater or water from a water butt in a clean container. Filter it through a coffee filter, pillowcase or sheet until it runs clear. Then boil it, or use water purification tablets. If you can't do either, add a quarter of a teaspoon of unscented household bleach for every {0} litres, and leave it for {1} minutes. Use this water for drinking only. Never drink flood water.

Signs of hypothermia

Shivering, cold and dry skin, blue or grey skin or lips (look at palms and soles on darker skin), slurred speech, slow breathing, tiredness or confusion. A baby may be cold to touch, floppy, unusually quiet and sleepy, and refuse to feed.
